title: VPC / On-Prem Upgrade Communications Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook provides copy-ready communication templates and a pragmatic sequence of steps for upgrades and maintenance windows for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is meant to be used by Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and the Private Deployments on-call when planning rolling upgrades, patching, or feature releases that touch control plane or data plane components.

Scope / When to use this playbook:
- Any planned upgrade that may change model runtime behavior, require a restart of services, modify network configuration, or change DB schema in the customer environment.
- Planned maintenance windows that may cause >100ms latency increase, brief 503 spikes, or scheduled per-node restarts.
- Emergency maintenance should follow the emergency comms template in the incident runbook (not covered here).

High-level communication cadence (recommended):
- Initial sync (Sales/CS --> Customer) when upgrade is scheduled: T-14 days
- Technical notice (with expected impact & prechecks): T-7 days
- Reminder + runbook & opt-out path: T-72 hours
- Day-of reminder (local business hours): T-24 hours
- 1 hour prior: short Slack/email reminder to ops contact
- Post-upgrade summary & validation: within 24 hours after completion

Impact categories and wording guidance:
- No user-visible impact: "No downtime expected. Background rolling upgrade; no action needed."
- Short window, targeted component: "We expect up to X minutes of degraded availability for <component>. Requests may be retried automatically."
- Brief interruptions across the cluster: "We anticipate a rolling restart with short interruptions (typically <5 minutes per node)."
- Planned downtime (full service interruption): "This upgrade requires a maintenance window where the service will be unavailable for approximately X minutes/hours."

Security + compliance snippet (always include in customer-facing notices):
- "This maintenance will not require Redwood access to your data plane. Any operations performed are under your control; logs and audit trails will be recorded in your environment per your configuration. If the upgrade requires us to access the control plane for coordination, we will do so via the previously agreed service account and will provide a post-action audit log."

Pre-upgrade technical checklist (should be run and logged into the Jira ticket):
- Confirm primary ops contact and escalation contacts (name, email, phone).
- Snapshot/backup: Verify last backup timestamp and retention location for DB and critical config (example DB snapshot id: {{db_snapshot_id}}).
- Terraform state access: Confirm team has access to remote state backend and lock is working.
- Test bucket/registry reachability: Confirm external artifacts (container registry, config store) are reachable from customer environment.
- Disk/IO and memory headroom: Ensure nodes have >= 30% free memory and disk for transient spikes.
- Time sync / NTP: Ensure system clocks within 5s drift.
- Canary node available: Reserve a node for canary validation if canary plan used.
- KMS/HSM keys: Confirm key access for secrets decryption if required.

Terraform module notes (concise guidance for infra owners and SE):
- Module versioning: Always pin module versions in the customer's root module, e.g., module.redwood_runtime.source = "github.com/redwood/terraform-modules//runtime?ref=v1.3.2".
- State migrations: If module changes require resource rename/move, provide a clear migration script using terraform state mv and record the mapping in the upgrade Jira ticket.
- Backend locking: Use S3/GCS backend with DynamoDB/Cloud Locking enabled. Confirm lock TTL and verify locks release after test plan.
- Provider upgrades: Run terraform plan in a sandbox and run provider upgrade in a dry-run workspace. Notify customer if provider requires reinitialization.
- Rollback: Keep previous module tag available; include terraform state snapshot before apply and store in the ticket.

Canary & rollout strategy (example):
- Step 0: Validate prechecks on all nodes (health, metrics).
- Step 1: Deploy to canary node (single node in a controlled AZ) and run smoke tests for 30 minutes.
- Step 2: If canary passes, proceed to rolling upgrade 10-20% nodes every 15-30 minutes depending on cluster size.
- Step 3: After each batch, run automated validation suite (see smoke tests below).
- Step 4: If any batch triggers SLO regression or critical errors, pause and rollback the last batch.

Validation (smoke tests) – run automated and manual checks after each batch:
- API health endpoints return 200 with <200ms median latency over 2 minutes.
- Token generation rate within ±10% of baseline.
- No increase in 5xx errors beyond agreed SLO thresholds (example SLO: 99th percentile latency < 400ms; error rate < 0.5%).
- Check KV cache hit-rate does not drop more than 15% during steady-state traffic.
- Basic inference sample: run 5 representative prompts and validate outputs for structural correctness (not full eval).

Rollback plan (minimal, practical):
- If a batch fails validation, start rollback within 10 minutes.
- Rollback steps: terraform apply using pinned previous module tag -> restart affected nodes -> run validation tests.
- If rollback is not immediately possible due to DB migration, escalate to on-call engineering with migration revert plan (see linked_confluence_page).

Customer-facing templates (editable)
1) Initial scheduling email (T-14 days)
Subject: Proposed maintenance window for Redwood Private deployment – {{customer_name}}
Body:
Hi {{customer_name}} team,

We’d like to schedule a planned upgrade to your Redwood Private deployment to deliver security updates and runtime improvements. Proposed window: {{date_range}} (UTC {{start}} – {{end}}).

Impact: Rolling upgrade; no expected data plane downtime for most upgrades. If a particular upgrade requires a brief maintenance window, we will indicate this in the technical notice.

Prechecks & coordination: Our SE, {{se_name}}, will run pre-upgrade checks with your ops contact, {{ops_name}}. If the proposed window does not work, please propose alternatives within 5 business days.

Regards,
Maya Patel (Private Deployments)

2) Technical notice (T-7 days)
Subject: Technical details & impact – Redwood maintenance for {{customer_name}} on {{date}}
Body:
Hello {{customer_name}} ops team,

This is the technical notice for the upcoming upgrade. Highlights:
- Components in scope: runtime (redwood-runtime), model cache, control-plane agent.
- Expected user impact: brief rolling restarts. Typical per-node interruption: 2–6 minutes.
- Terraform/infra changes: module redwood_runtime v1.3.2 -> v1.4.0 (state migration required).

Required action: Please confirm backup snapshot id and that you have a contact available during the window. If you require a dry-run in a staging environment prior to the upgrade, let us know.

Security note: No secret keys will be transferred outside your environment unless explicitly authorized.

3) Reminder (T-72 hours)
Subject: Reminder – Redwood upgrade on {{date}} ({{window}})
Body: short bullet list with contact and minimal impact description plus opt-out instruction and reschedule link.

4) Day-of short message (T-1 hour)
Slack/email: "Starting rolling upgrade for Redwood runtime in {{region}}. SE: {{se_name}}. Expected per-node restart ~3–5min. If you see a 503 spike, please hold retries for 60s and contact ops."

Post-upgrade summary (example)
Subject: Post-upgrade summary – Redwood maintenance {{date}}
Body:
Hi {{customer_name}},

Upgrade completed at {{completion_time}} (UTC). Summary:
- What changed: runtime v1.4.0 (perf and security fixes) + terraform module update.
- Impact observed: brief 503 spikes for 9 minutes total during canary; rolling upgrade held for 20m and resumed.
- Validation: all smoke tests passed; 99th latency at 370ms (pre-upgrade baseline 360ms).
- Rollback used: none required.

Artifacts: Terraform plan and applied diff: {{link}}. Runbook and logs: {{link}}.

If you observe any anomalies, reply to this thread and we’ll triage immediately.

Escalation contacts (order, include phone and pager)
- Primary SE: {{se_name}} – se+pd@redwood.ai / +1-555-0199
- On-call private deployments engineer: oncall-private@redwood.ai / Pager: +1-555-0200
- SRE escalation: sre-esc@redwood.ai

Communications handling tips for CS/SE:
- Be explicit about what is required from the customer and what Redwood will perform.
- When in doubt, include a single-sentence TL;DR at top of any notice.
- Always include the opt-out/reschedule path and threshold for rescheduling (e.g., cannot reschedule <72 hours).
- Attach verification artifacts (terraform plan, state snapshot id) to the Jira ticket.

Templates for different channels:
- Email: full context + attachments + action items.
- Slack DM: short, link to ticket, include ops contact and SE.
- Portal notice (if customer uses console): short banner + link to details.

Edge cases & special considerations:
- Air-gapped environments: Pre-stage all artifacts in customer registry and include explicit checksum values in notice.
- Customers with strict maintenance windows: honor specified windows; require 30+ days lead-time for DB migrations.
- Regulatory customers: include compliance officer cc and provide evidence of audit logs post-upgrade.

Example checkboxes for the ticket description (copy into Jira):
- [ ] Ops contact confirmed
- [ ] Backup verified: snapshot id {{db_snapshot_id}}
- [ ] Terraform state snapshot saved: {{tf_state_snapshot}}
- [ ] Canary node reserved
- [ ] KMS access validated
- [ ] Smoke tests defined and linked
- [ ] Communication templates sent on schedule

Appendix A — quick Terraform commands for state snapshot (share with infra owner):
- terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
- terraform state pull > state-{{date}}.json
- aws s3 cp state-{{date}}.json s3://redwood-tf-state-backups/{{customer}}/state-{{date}}.json

Appendix B — minimal post-upgrade verification script (bash):
- curl -sS -I https://{{customer_api}}/health | grep 200
- run_small_infer_check --endpoint https://{{customer_api}}/v1/generate --prompt "hello" --expect-structure
- prometheus_query "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))"

Notes / open questions to resolve before finalizing template:
- Confirm opt-out policy for customers on long-term support contracts (LTS).
- Agree on SLO thresholds for customers with custom SLAs; include in customer profile in CRM.
- Define exact notification localization workflow for non-English locales.
- Confirm whether Redwood should post-run aggregated anonymized upgrade metrics to customers for benchmarking.

Change log:
- 2025-11-04: Initial draft (Maya Patel)
- 2026-02-18: Added Terraform state snapshot guidance and canary timings (Oliver Chen)
- 2026-03-10: Expanded rollback procedure and added post-upgrade verification script (Priya Rao)

End of document.
